testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system use?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: All air tanks must have:
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must have drain valves. These valves remove water and oil that collect in the tanks. They can be operated manually or automatically.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the brake pedal
The distance between the brake pedal's resting position and the floor
The amount of air pressure used to stop a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through brake lines. Air brakes do not work instantly. There is usually at least half a second between pressing the pedal and the brakes starting to work. Hydraulic brakes work right away.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. Two separate braking systems work from one set of controls. Each system brakes different axles.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes:
questions.explanation: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, press down on the brake pedal.

questions.question: What must happen before air pressure in an air brake tank drops below 55 psi?

options.text: The warning light should turn on.
The vehicle will be unable to shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light should turn on.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light must turn on before air pressure drops below 55 psi. If this warning does not work during an inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too noisy.
Air brake systems work very well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air brake systems work very well.
questions.explanation: Air brakes are effective and safe for large, heavy vehicles when they are maintained and used correctly.

questions.question: Not draining air tanks could cause:

options.text: Water to freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water to freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: The emergency brake system is made up of:

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: a service brake system, a parking brake system, and an emergency brake system. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes used?

options.text: Only at the driver's side wheels.

questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are used at all four wheels. The most common type is the S-cam drum brake.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Makes the vehicle stop in a shorter distance.
Makes it harder to control the vehicle.
Gives you better control of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you better control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents the wheels from locking up during hard braking. This gives you better control. However, ABS does not always make the vehicle stop in a shorter distance.

questions.question: When can brakes go out of adjustment?

options.text: When one side is used more than the other side.

questions.explanation: Brakes often go out of adjustment when they are hot. Use proper braking techniques to keep your brakes from overheating.

questions.question: What gets removed when you drain an air tank?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If left in the system, water and oil can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Why should you drain the air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced.
Because compressed air contains water that builds up in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that builds up in the tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and compressor oil that can build up in the air storage tanks and damage the brake system. Drain the tanks daily to remove these materials. Use the manual drain valve at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: What should you do if the low air pressure warning comes on?

options.text: Keep driving and have the brakes fixed within a week.
Pull over and check the brakes.
Call a mechanic while you are driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on while driving a vehicle with air brakes, stop the vehicle right away while you can still control the brakes. Check and fix the brakes as soon as possible.

questions.question: How should air tank drains be used?

options.text: The driver should not use them.
Only use them when it is wet outside.
Use them to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use them to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and compressor oil. If left in the system, water and oil can damage the brakes. Open the manual drain valves daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What allows a driver to slowly apply spring brakes?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve allows a driver to slowly apply spring brakes. In equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls this valve.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three systems: the service brake, the parking brake, and the emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: At what air pressure level does an air compressor governor stop the compressor?
questions.explanation: An air compressor governor stops the compressor from pumping air when the air tanks reach 125 psi. This level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve protects air tanks and the air brake system. It opens at 150 psi to prevent too much pressure from building up.

questions.question: You are braking on dry pavement at 55 mph. How much extra distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your stopping distance.

questions.question: Brakes can get out of adjustment if:
questions.explanation: Brakes can get out of adjustment quickly if they overheat from heavy use. Check your brake adjustment often.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?
questions.explanation: Large trucks use air brake systems. These systems use compressed air to operate the brakes.

questions.question: An emergency brake must be controlled by:
questions.explanation: All trucks and buses must have emergency and parking brakes. These brakes must use mechanical force because air pressure can leak away over time.
